QF.id: AIFM CII Fund Performance and Benchmarking_34

question.text: Mr. Raghav Mehta is the sole Managing Partner of Nalanda Growth AIF (Cat II). If he becomes incapacitated and the Investment Manager entity cannot continue operations, under SEBI's Liquidation Schemes circular the Fund:

answer.text: Must continue unchanged; LPs have no rights.
Converts to a perpetual open-ended fund.
Automatically transfers to a government-designated trustee bank with full continuation.
May be required to liquidate its assets during the winding-up process; Fund may not realise full value of investments.

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Section 7.2 'Dependence on Investment Manager': 'If the Investment Manager cannot continue to manage the Fund, due to bankruptcy or dissolution, the Fund may liquidate its assets during the winding-up process, as per the SEBI circulars on Liquidation Schemes. Further, if members of the key investment team cease…, the quality of investment management services may be adversely affected. In such cases, it might not be possible to realize the full value of the investments.' The Trap: A ignores SEBI's liquidation framework. C is fictitious. D — Cat I/II cannot be open-ended. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C and XIX-A test dependency-on-IM risk. SEBI's 2023 liquidation-scheme circular provides the mechanism. Manager's Pro-Tip: Build a 'Deputy Managing Partner' succession line into the Investment Manager entity's constitutional documents — a named successor shortens the liquidation-risk window from 18+ months to under 6 months for LPs.
